captive_summary: Two gas-fired power facilities sit at/near the Sodegaura LNG terminal, and neither is captive to it. (1) JERA's large legacy Sodegaura Thermal Power Station (Unit 1 from 1974, being replaced 2032-2041 with GTCC units) is a major grid-supply utility station fed by the terminal — direction-OUT, already reflected in GEM's power_plants_supplied field. (2) Tokyo Gas completed its own "Sodegaura Power Plant" (10 gas engines, 97,800 kW total) on the LNG terminal grounds in March 2025, but Tokyo Gas's own press release states its purpose is explicitly commercial grid-balancing/ancillary services for renewable-energy integration, not powering the terminal's own operations.
confirmed_how: Tokyo Gas's own March 2025 completion press release states the plant will be used "as one of the adjustment capabilities to respond to market volatility caused by fluctuations in renewable energy output and electric power demand, thereby contributing to system stabilization" — a commercial grid-support function, not terminal self-supply. Japanese Wikipedia on Sodegaura Thermal Power Station corroborates that the large adjacent station is JERA's own utility-scale generating asset (legacy since 1974, undergoing GTCC replacement), i.e. an outbound fuel-supply relationship, not captive.
